title: Best Buy sells Blu-rays online and in-store again
gist: Best Buy has resumed first-party Blu-ray sales online and in stores (15 titles 'sold & shipped by Best Buy') after announcing in October 2023 that it would exit disc sales starting in 2024 (the opening line says it exited in 2023). The reversal comes as overall US disc spending fell 9.3% in 2024-2025 while 4K Blu-ray spending rose 12%, driven by collectors, SteelBooks, Gen Z and distrust of revocable digital 'purchases'.

insights.claim: Best Buy is again selling Blu-rays directly through its website and physical stores, with 15 Blu-rays (including one two-pack) listed as 'sold & shipped by Best Buy', including 2026 releases such as The Odyssey and Project Hail Mary.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A major electronics retailer reversing a physical-media exit is a signal that the premium disc niche is commercially viable again.
insights.quote: The Best Buy website’s movie section currently lists 15 Blu-rays (including one two-pack) that are “sold & shipped by Best Buy.”

insights.claim: In October 2023 Best Buy announced it would stop selling Blu-rays and DVDs online and in stores starting in 2024, citing changing viewing habits and wanting floor space for new tech.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Context for the reversal: the exit rationale (streaming shift, shelf space) has been partly overtaken by niche demand.
insights.quote: Making this change gives us more space and opportunity to bring customers new and innovative tech for them to explore, discover and enjoy

insights.claim: Before resuming first-party sales, Best Buy's website began selling Blu-rays and DVDs from third parties via its online marketplace last year, a lower-risk way to test disc demand.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Marketplace-first then first-party is a pattern for retailers re-entering niche categories without inventory risk up front.

insights.claim: Best Buy's Blu-ray offering is mostly online with ship-to-home or store pickup within days, though new releases like The Odyssey appear to be stocked in stores for pickup within an hour.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Limited in-store stocking suggests a cautious, inventory-light re-entry rather than a full category relaunch.
insights.locator: Most of the Blu-rays are available for purchase

insights.claim: Many companies have cut back physical media: Target sells discs in stores only on special occasions, Disney outsourced its DVD and Blu-ray business to Sony, Sony stopped selling recordable Blu-rays to consumers, and Redbox went out of business.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Retail and studio retreat thins supply, which can leave remaining sellers with less competition in a smaller but loyal market.

insights.claim: US consumer spending on Blu-rays and DVDs fell 9.3 percent from 2024 to 2025, according to the Digital Entertainment Group, continuing a steady decline.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Physical media overall remains a shrinking category; any upside is concentrated in premium segments.
insights.locator: Overall, the sales of Blu-rays and DVDs

insights.claim: While total US disc spending fell, consumer spending on 4K Blu-ray discs rose 12 percent year over year from 2024 to 2025, per the Digital Entertainment Group.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Premiumization: the high-end format is growing inside a declining category, favoring studios/labels and retailers focused on 4K and collectibles.
insights.quote: consumer spending on 4K Blu-ray discs specifically increased 12 percent year over year

insights.claim: Physical media enthusiasts rely on discs because digital movies 'purchased' online can be removed from libraries without warning, and because discs offer better picture and sound quality than digital versions.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Digital-ownership revocation risk is a structural demand driver for physical media and a reputational risk for digital storefronts.
insights.quote: digital copies of movies and shows can be plucked from online platforms and people’s libraries that were previously “purchased” (but truly only rented) without warning

insights.claim: A resurgence in Blu-ray sales has been associated with collectible SteelBook editions and with Gen Z buyers, some of whom are even using video rental stores.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Collectible packaging and young-buyer nostalgia support higher price points; watch for retailers and labels leaning into limited editions.

insights.claim: Criterion president Peter Becker said there is a lot of evidence that more young people are thinking about physical media differently, as on-demand abundance makes ownership more important.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Boutique labels see a durable youth-driven collector market, supporting the niche thesis behind Best Buy's return.
